Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the TrendMart Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the listen-only portion of the call. Should you require operator assistance during this time, please press star then zero on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Mike Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to TrendMart's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Jordan Lee, COO; and Taylor Kim, CMO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson, CEO of TrendMart.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, Mike, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by exceptional mobile app engagement with record downloads and user activity boosting conversions, alongside meaningful take rate expansion from smarter pricing and promotions. We saw significant growth in key metrics, including GMV up 24% year-over-year to $30.2 billion and active buyers reaching 85 million.

Our focus remains on accelerating seller services adoption, which powered high-margin revenue streams and strengthened our marketplace ecosystem. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our AI-enhanced value-added services like premium logistics and advertising tools, which we believe will significantly enhance overall profitability.

We are investing heavily in operational efficiencies, particularly around fulfillment to drive down costs per order while scaling delivery speeds.

Finally, we are committed to optimizing customer acquisition through efficient marketing channels that deliver superior ROI.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $15.2 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, driven by take rate improvements, higher adoption of seller services, and a favorable product mix leaning toward higher-margin categories like electronics. Operating expenses were $6.8 billion, representing 45% of revenue, with disciplined control across the board despite investments in growth areas.

Marketing spend came in at $285 million, or about 1.9% of revenue, reflecting strong efficiency gains that I'll touch on shortly.

Our net income for the quarter was $1.2 billion, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $8.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue between $65 billion and $68 billion, adjusted EBITDA margins of 18-20%, and continued take rate expansion.

To give you deeper insight into the drivers behind these results, let me start with our mobile app engagement metrics—downloads, active users, and conversion rates—which are central to our growth strategy, especially as mobile now drives over 60% of global e-commerce traffic according to recent Statista data.

On downloads, we hit 4.8 million new installs across iOS and Android in Q3, a solid 28% year-over-year increase and 12% quarter-over-quarter. This pushes our cumulative total to 185 million worldwide. Key to this was our App Store Optimization efforts, landing us in the top 10 Shopping apps in the US and UK on both Apple and Google Play. Geo-targeted campaigns using Apple Search Ads and Google Universal App Campaigns kept our cost per install at a low $1.42, improved 15% sequentially via machine learning targeting high lifetime value users. That's better than peers like Shein, who manage around $2.00 CPI.

For active users, monthly actives reached a record 28.2 million, up 22% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, with dailies at 9.1 million for a healthy 32% DAU/MAU ratio—above the 25-28% e-commerce average from App Annie. Retention improved across the board: 48% on day 1, 32% on day 7, and 18% on day 30, gaining 5 points year-over-year. Our ShopLoop personalized feed, mimicking Instagram Reels with algorithm-curated products, extended sessions by 18% to 6.2 minutes average. North America leads with 55% of MAUs at 15.5 million, Europe 25% or 7 million with gains in Germany and France after localized launches, APAC at 15% or 4.2 million surging 40% in India and Southeast Asia on smartphone growth, and LATAM at 5% or 1.4 million up 35% despite currency swings.

Conversion rates from app sessions hit 4.7%, more than 4 times our 1.1% mobile web rate and ahead of desktop's 2.9%, powering $1.2 billion in app GMV or 52% of total Q3 GMV, up from 45% last year. One-tap checkout with Apple Pay, Google Pay, and FastCart wallet cut abandonment 22% to 65%, while add-to-cart rose 14% to 12.5% via dynamic pricing and personalized push notifications yielding 3.5x open rates, like restock alerts for fashion.

We've bounced back from iOS 14.5 App Tracking Transparency challenges using first-party data and SKAdNetwork 4.0 for 85% attribution recovery, similar to Amazon's approach. Back-to-school helped electronics conversions jump 30% month-over-month, though inflation kept AOV flat at $68 versus $72 last year—still, app ARPU at $42.70 is 20% above web.

Tech-wise, the v5.2 update added AR try-on via Snapchat Lens Studio and voice search with Google Dialogflow, boosting Gen Z engagement 25%—they're now 32% of DAUs. Beta Web3 wallet for NFT loyalty aims for 10% retention lift. We're allocating $25 million in FY24 capex for edge computing to drop load times under 1.5 seconds, as 53% abandon carts over 3 seconds per Google.

This app-first strategy cuts CAC 30% to $18 per user from $32 web and lifts LTV 2.5x via repeats. Targeting 35 million MAUs by year-end with conversions over 5%, via TikTok Shop in APAC and Mercado Libre in LATAM. Risks like Android fragmentation or Play billing changes persist, but our 70/30 share model helps.

Next, our take rate, the share of GMV we capture via commissions, fulfillment, ads, and services like NexLogistics and NexAds. Blended take rate rose to 22.5% in Q3, up 150 basis points year-over-year from 21.0% and 40 basis points from Q2's 22.1%, adding about $180 million to revenue on $28.5 billion GMV—strongest expansion since late 2021.

Pricing discipline led: Standard 15% commissions on fashion stay competitive versus Etsy's 6.5% plus payments, but Premium Seller Program adds 200 basis points for AI placement and perks, with 45% adoption up from 32%, lifting 60 basis points. Fulfillment fees up 8% on carrier costs from UPS/FedEx port issues, net +90 basis points despite volume discounts; seller churn flat at 4.2%, net adds 150,000 to 2.8 million total.

Promotions smarter now: Shifted to NexPromo Engine capping apparel discounts at 25% from 40%, cutting promo drag from 2.2% to 1.3% of GMV for +80 basis points. Core take excluding promos at 23.8%; contrasts Shein/Temu's 50%+ offs at 15-18% takes.

Mix shifts added +30 basis points: Electronics/home at 28% take grew to 32% GMV on back-to-school, fashion dipped to 25%. Prime members (65 million, +12%) drove 55% GMV at 24.5% take versus 19% non-Prime.

Tech like Dynamic Take Rate Optimizer personalizes fees, boosting ads to 4.8% GMV (+50 basis points), NexChain blockchain cuts disputes 30% for 1% logistics upsell, +40 basis points total.

Regionally: North America (65% GMV) 20.8% (+120 bps), Europe (20%) 24.2% (+200 bps) on VAT ads, APAC (12%) 26.5% (+180 bps) via Shanghai hub, ROW (3%) 22.0%.

Q4 guide 23.0-23.5%, toward 25% by FY2026 for 25%+ EBITDA margins. Piloting 30-35% enterprise tiers with Nike-like brands, $500M AI capex for 200 bps uplift. Temu low-pricing, EU regs risks mitigated.

Turning to seller services and value-added services—or VAS—this high-margin stream hit 28% of net revenue, up from 22%, with $4.2 billion in Q3, +35% year-over-year. At 75%+ gross margins, it drove EBITDA to 18.2%.

On 2.8 million sellers and $180 billion GMV (+22%), VAS includes ads, FBN logistics, NexPay, analytics, AI inventory tools. 68% sellers use at least one, up from 52%.

FBN: 62% adoption, 1.7 million sellers, 1.2 billion units (45% total), $1.8 billion revenue +42%, ARPU $1,250 +15%; 95% US two-day Prime, 85% EU.

Ads: 41% adoption, $1.5 billion +38%, 18% take, 450 billion impressions +55%, 4.2x ROAS via DSP ML.

Payments: NexPay $120 billion at 2.1% fee, 55% adoption; NexInsights 32%, Brand Registry +25%.

Outpaces Shopify ~40%, Alibaba ~50%. VAS drove 65% revenue growth, take on third-party GMV to 12.8% from 10.9%; 76% margins vs. retail 3x lower.

North America 72% adoption $2.9B +40%, Europe 58% $650M +28%, APAC 65% $450M +55% on UPI India, China rebound.

Trends: Mobile sellers 75% new, enterprise bundles +28% ARPU. GenAI Copilot +25% conversions for 500K users, blockchain fraud -40%.

Targets 75% adoption 2025, Q4 $4.5-4.7B +33-38%, FY take 13.2%. Ecosystem lock-in churn <8%.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan to discuss operations.

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Sarah. Operationally, we focused on fulfillment efficiencies and network optimization. Our shipping times improved by 25% year-over-year, with 95% of US orders hitting two-day Prime. Fulfillment costs per order—or FCPO—trended down to $7.42, a 12% year-over-year drop from $8.45 and 5% sequential from $7.81—10th straight quarter of declines, trailing 12-month at $7.68, or 14.2% of revenue versus 16.8%. With AOV at $48.20 up 3% on recs, this adds 120 basis points to EBITDA, better than Shopify's ~$9.50.

FulfillFast 2.0 ($250M invested): Robotics in 85% of 45 NA FCs cut pick times 35% to <30 seconds, labor to 38%; Dallas mega-FC 1,200 picks/hour/associate.

Dynamic routing with UPS/FedEx/GXO optimizes 92%, saves 18 cents on 6-8% hikes, 15% discounts. NA $6.95 (68% GMV), Europe €8.10/$8.75 (22% GMV, micro-FCs), APAC ¥650/$4.60 (10% GMV).

Returns down to 18% from 24%, costs -22% via AI right-sizing, virtual try-ons; 65% inbound processing saves $1.20/return.

Enables Prime ramp to 45% orders, 5,000 new sellers. Pilots autonomous/Starship drones for 10-15% cuts by 2026. Sub-$8 positions us vs. Amazon $10+.

We are implementing AI-orchestrated micro-fulfillment in 20 new metros.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from our social video campaigns and SEO initiatives. Customer acquisition costs were $42.50, down 18% year-over-year. Our brand awareness increased by 35% per recent surveys. We are focusing on performance partnerships and retention-led growth.

Blended CAC at $42.50, -18% from $52 YoY, flat sequential from $43, despite +22% new customers to 6.7 million—below $50-60 peer average for apparel DTC like Everlane.

Paid media (45% spend): Google/Meta 5.2x ROAS + from 4.1x, ML on Performance Max/Advantage+; search CAC -15% on keywords like sustainable athleisure, TikTok UGC 6.8x at $38 CAC.

Organic/SEO 22% adds sub-$20 CAC: Headless Shopify speed -14% bounce, 450 content clusters +31% traffic, long-tail +40% conversions.

Payback 4.8 months from 6.2, LTV $285 +12% for 6.7:1 ratio, mROI 4.8x via BigQuery CDP.

NA $39 (62% rev), APAC $58 high LTV $420 live-stream beta -22%, Europe $52 cookieless stable 4.1x.

AI NovaAI 1,200 cohorts +25% email to $15 CAC, affiliates 5,000 creators $28/7x, referrals 12% $18 viral 1.4.

Q4 ~$45 on holidays, FY 8M adds at 22% rev marketing, 4.5x ROAS MMM.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [Standard operator instructions]. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Sarah, could you expand on how the take rate expansion is sustainable given competitive pricing pressures from players like Temu?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, John. Absolutely, sustainability comes from our pricing discipline and tech like the Dynamic Optimizer, which has already added 50 basis points in tests without hurting retention—churn flat at 4.2%. We're not chasing volume at all costs; smart promos and mix shifts position us for 23-23.5% in Q4, balancing 18-20% GMV growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. Taylor, on CAC—how are you managing the holiday uptick while scaling APAC?

Taylor Kim:
Hi Emily. Holiday CPMs are up 15% already, but dynamic allocation via MMM keeps us at 4.5x ROAS. In APAC, live-streaming betas dropped CAC 22%, leveraging higher AOV for strong LTV payback despite higher upfront costs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel:
Thanks. Jordan, impressive FCPO—any color on the robotics rollout timeline and Europe challenges?

Jordan Lee:
David, robotics now at 85% NA FCs, expanding to Europe next year with micro-FCs countering VAT/ESG hurdles—already down 9% YoY there. Full pilots for drones/autonomous by mid-2025 targeting further 10% cuts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays.

Lisa Wong:
Congrats team. Sarah, seller services adoption hit 68%—what's driving VAS acceleration in APAC?

Sarah Chen:
Lisa, thanks. APAC VAS up 55% to $450 million on 65% adoption, fueled by UPI payments in India mirroring Amazon Pay, and localized logistics amid Red Sea issues. GenAI Copilot adds 25% uplift, targeting 75% overall by 2025.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Thompson for closing remarks.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
